ashkenaz_338.name: Ashkenaz
ashkenaz_338.who: A son of Gomer and great-grandson of Noah through Japheth, listed in the Table of Nations.
key: He is listed among the sons of Gomer, son of Japheth (Genesis 10).
Chronicles repeats his name in the line of Japheth (1 Chronicles 1).
Later a kingdom called Ashkenaz is summoned with others against Babylon (Jeremiah 51).

atarah_354.name: Atarah
atarah_354.who: A wife of Jerahmeel of the tribe of Judah and the mother of Onam.
key: She is named as another wife of Jerahmeel, Hezron's firstborn son (1 Chronicles 2).
She bore Onam, whose descendants are traced in Judah's genealogy (1 Chronicles 2).

azaniah_368.name: Azaniah
azaniah_368.who: A Levite whose son Jeshua sealed the covenant in Nehemiah's day.
key: He is named as the father of the Levite Jeshua (Nehemiah 10).
His son Jeshua was among the Levites who set their seal on the covenant to keep God's law (Nehemiah 10).

azariah_2925.name: Azariah
azariah_2925.who: A Kohathite Levite listed among the ancestors of Heman, David's temple singer.
key: He appears in Heman's ancestry as son of Zephaniah and father of Joel (1 Chronicles 6).
The parallel list of Kohath's descendants appears to call him Uzziah son of Uriel (1 Chronicles 6).
His descendant Heman led the singers whom David appointed for the house of the LORD (1 Chronicles 6).

azariah_373.name: Azariah
azariah_373.who: A priest in Aaron's line, son of Ahimaaz and grandson of Zadok, in the days of Solomon.
key: He is listed in the high priestly line as son of Ahimaaz and father of Johanan (1 Chronicles 6).
He is possibly the Azariah son of Zadok named first among Solomon's high officials (1 Kings 4).

azariah_378.name: Azariah
azariah_378.who: A priest in Aaron's line, son of Johanan, noted as serving in Solomon's temple.
key: He is listed in the high priestly line as son of Johanan and father of Amariah (1 Chronicles 6).
Chronicles notes he served as priest in the house Solomon built in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 6).
He is named among the ancestors of Ezra the priest and scribe (Ezra 7).

azariah_379.name: Azariah
azariah_379.who: A priest in Aaron's line, son of the high priest Hilkiah and grandfather of Jehozadak.
key: He is listed in the high priestly line as son of Hilkiah and father of Seraiah (1 Chronicles 6).
His son Seraiah's son Jehozadak went into exile when the LORD sent Judah away (1 Chronicles 6).
He is named among the ancestors of Ezra the priest and scribe (Ezra 7).

azariah_380.name: Azariah
azariah_380.who: A prophet, son of Oded, who encouraged King Asa of Judah to seek the LORD.
key: The Spirit of God came on him, and he went out to meet Asa after a victory (2 Chronicles 15).
He told Asa the LORD is with them while they are with him (2 Chronicles 15).
Asa took courage, removed idols, and led Judah in a covenant to seek the LORD (2 Chronicles 15).

azariah_385.name: Azariah
azariah_385.who: The chief priest who confronted King Uzziah when the king entered the temple to burn incense.
key: With eighty priests he withstood Uzziah, saying burning incense belonged to the consecrated priests (2 Chronicles 26).
Leprosy broke out on Uzziah's forehead, and Azariah and the priests rushed him out (2 Chronicles 26).

azubah_568.name: Azubah
azubah_568.who: A wife of Caleb son of Hezron in the genealogy of Judah.
key: Caleb fathered children by his wife Azubah (1 Chronicles 2).
After Azubah died, Caleb married Ephrath, who bore him Hur (1 Chronicles 2).

baal-zebub_579.name: Baal-zebub
baal-zebub_579.who: A Philistine god worshiped at Ekron, consulted by King Ahaziah of Israel.
key: Injured in a fall, Ahaziah sent messengers to ask Baal-zebub whether he would recover (2 Kings 1).
Elijah rebuked the king for not inquiring of Israel's God and announced his death (2 Kings 1).

baal_574.name: Baal
baal_574.who: A man of the tribe of Reuben listed in the genealogy of Joel's descendants.
key: He is listed in Reuben's line as son of Reaiah and father of Beerah (1 Chronicles 5).
His son Beerah, a Reubenite chief, was carried into exile by Tiglath-pileser of Assyria (1 Chronicles 5).

baana_580.name: Baana
baana_580.who: Son of Ahilud and one of Solomon's twelve district officers who provided food for the king.
key: He governed Solomon's district of Taanach, Megiddo, and Beth-shean, as far as Abel-meholah (1 Kings 4).
Like the other officers, he supplied provisions for the king's household one month each year (1 Kings 4).

baanah_582.name: Baanah
baanah_582.who: A Benjaminite raiding captain who, with his brother Rechab, murdered Ish-bosheth, Saul's son.
key: He and Rechab, sons of Rimmon of Beeroth, led raiding bands for Ish-bosheth (2 Samuel 4).
They entered Ish-bosheth's house at midday, killed him on his bed, and took his head (2 Samuel 4).
They brought the head to David at Hebron, expecting a reward (2 Samuel 4).
David condemned them for killing a righteous man and had them executed (2 Samuel 4).

barachel_400.name: Barachel
barachel_400.who: A Buzite of the family of Ram and the father of Elihu, Job's young counselor.
key: He is named as the father of Elihu, of the family of Ram (Job 32).
His son Elihu spoke in anger after Job's three friends fell silent (Job 32).

bartimaeus_406.name: Bartimaeus
bartimaeus_406.who: A blind beggar near Jericho, son of Timaeus, whom Jesus healed on his way to Jerusalem.
key: Sitting by the road at Jericho, he cried out to Jesus, Son of David, for mercy (Mark 10).
Many rebuked him, but he cried out all the more, and Jesus called him (Mark 10).
Throwing off his cloak, he came and asked to recover his sight (Mark 10).
Jesus said his faith had made him well; he saw and followed Jesus on the way (Mark 10).

ben-ammi_451.name: Ben-ammi
ben-ammi_451.who: The son of Lot by his younger daughter and the ancestor of the Ammonites.
key: After Sodom's destruction, Lot's younger daughter conceived by her father in a cave near Zoar (Genesis 19).
She bore a son, named him Ben-ammi, and he became the father of the Ammonites (Genesis 19).

ben-hadad_453.name: Ben-hadad
ben-hadad_453.who: A king of Syria in Elisha's day who besieged Samaria and was later murdered by Hazael.
key: He mustered his army and besieged Samaria, causing a terrible famine in the city (2 Kings 6).
Falling sick, he sent Hazael to ask Elisha whether he would recover (2 Kings 8).
The next day Hazael smothered him with a wet cloth and became king (2 Kings 8).

ben-hadad_454.name: Ben-hadad
ben-hadad_454.who: A king of Syria, son of Hazael, who oppressed Israel until King Jehoash defeated him.
key: The LORD gave Israel into the hands of Hazael and his son Ben-hadad (2 Kings 13).
He became king after Hazael died (2 Kings 13).
Jehoash of Israel defeated him three times and recovered the cities Hazael had taken (2 Kings 13).
Amos announced that fire would devour the strongholds of Ben-hadad (Amos 1).

benaiah_440.name: Benaiah
benaiah_440.who: A warrior from Pirathon in Ephraim, one of David's mighty men and a division commander.
key: Benaiah of Pirathon is listed among David's Thirty, his elite warriors (2 Samuel 23).
Chronicles includes him among David's mighty men as well (1 Chronicles 11).
He commanded David's army division of 24,000 men for the eleventh month (1 Chronicles 27).

benaiah_443.name: Benaiah
benaiah_443.who: The father of Jehoiada, who became one of David's counselors after Ahithophel.
key: His son Jehoiada succeeded Ahithophel as one of David's counselors (1 Chronicles 27).
He is likely Benaiah son of Jehoiada, commander of David's bodyguard, listed earlier (1 Chronicles 27).

benjamin_458.name: Benjamin
benjamin_458.who: A descendant of Jacob's son Benjamin, son of Bilhan, listed in his tribe's genealogy.
key: He is listed among the sons of Bilhan in the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 7).
Bilhan's descendants included 17,200 mighty warriors ready for war (1 Chronicles 7).

benjamin_460.name: Benjamin
benjamin_460.who: A man of Jerusalem who helped rebuild the city wall under Nehemiah.
key: He and Hasshub repaired the section of wall opposite their house (Nehemiah 3).
His work was part of the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls led by Nehemiah (Nehemiah 3).

benjamin_461.name: Benjamin
benjamin_461.who: One of the leaders who joined the procession at the dedication of Jerusalem's rebuilt wall.
key: He went with the leaders of Judah behind the first thanksgiving choir on the wall (Nehemiah 12).
The people rejoiced at the dedication, and the joy was heard far away (Nehemiah 12).

berechiah_475.name: Berechiah
berechiah_475.who: The son of Iddo and father of the post-exilic prophet Zechariah.
key: The word of the LORD came to his son Zechariah in Darius's second year (Zechariah 1).
Ezra calls Zechariah the son of Iddo, naming his grandfather (Ezra 5).

beriah_479.name: Beriah
beriah_479.who: A son of Ephraim, born after two of Ephraim's sons were killed by the men of Gath.
key: Ephraim's sons Ezer and Elead were killed raiding Gath's livestock, and Ephraim mourned many days (1 Chronicles 7).
Ephraim's wife then bore a son, named Beriah because disaster had come on the house (1 Chronicles 7).

bernice_482.name: Bernice
bernice_482.who: A royal woman who accompanied King Agrippa when he heard Paul's defense in Caesarea.
key: She arrived with Agrippa at Caesarea to greet the new governor Festus (Acts 25).
She entered the audience hall with Agrippa amid great pomp to hear Paul (Acts 25).
After Paul spoke, she rose with the king and governor, and they agreed he deserved no death (Acts 26).

bilhan_503.name: Bilhan
bilhan_503.who: A Horite of Seir, son of the chief Ezer, listed among Edom's early inhabitants.
key: He is listed among the sons of Ezer, a Horite chief in the land of Seir (Genesis 36).
Chronicles repeats him among the descendants of Seir (1 Chronicles 1).

bunah_525.name: Bunah
bunah_525.who: A son of Jerahmeel, Hezron's firstborn, in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah.
key: He is listed among the sons of Jerahmeel with Ram, Oren, Ozem, and Ahijah (1 Chronicles 2).
His father Jerahmeel was the firstborn son of Hezron, grandson of Judah (1 Chronicles 2).

cainan_535.name: Cainan
cainan_535.who: A son of Arphaxad and father of Shelah, named in Luke's genealogy of Jesus.
key: Luke lists him between Arphaxad and Shelah in the ancestry of Jesus (Luke 3).
Genesis names Shelah directly as Arphaxad's son, without listing Cainan (Genesis 11).

carchemish_925.name: Carchemish
carchemish_925.who: A city on the Euphrates, not a person, where Pharaoh Neco went to fight.
key: Josiah went out against Neco, who was marching to fight at Carchemish (2 Chronicles 35).
Josiah was wounded by archers and died (2 Chronicles 35).

carmi_921.name: Carmi
carmi_921.who: A man of Judah, son of Zabdi, whose son Achan brought trouble on Israel at Jericho.
key: He is named as son of Zabdi, of the clan of Zerah in Judah (Joshua 7).
His son Achan took devoted things from Jericho and was found out by lot (Joshua 7).
Chronicles calls his son Achar, the troubler of Israel (1 Chronicles 2).

chenaanah_932.name: Chenaanah
chenaanah_932.who: The father of Zedekiah, a false prophet in King Ahab's court.
key: His son Zedekiah made iron horns and promised Ahab victory over Syria (1 Kings 22).
Zedekiah son of Chenaanah struck the prophet Micaiah on the cheek (2 Chronicles 18).

chimham_941.name: Chimham
chimham_941.who: A man who went to Jerusalem with King David in place of the aged Barzillai.
key: Barzillai asked David to take his servant Chimham in his place (2 Samuel 19).
David promised to do for Chimham whatever Barzillai wished, and Chimham went on with the king (2 Samuel 19).
A lodging place near Bethlehem was later called Geruth Chimham (Jeremiah 41).

claudius_947.name: Claudius
claudius_947.who: The Roman emperor during part of the early church's spread, mentioned twice in Acts.
key: Agabus foretold a great famine, which took place in the days of Claudius (Acts 11).
Claudius commanded all the Jews to leave Rome, so Aquila and Priscilla came to Corinth (Acts 18).

cozbi_959.name: Cozbi
cozbi_959.who: A Midianite woman, daughter of the chief Zur, killed with Zimri by Phinehas at Peor.
key: Zimri brought her into the camp in the sight of Moses while Israel wept (Numbers 25).
Phinehas pierced them both with a spear, and the plague on Israel stopped (Numbers 25).
The LORD cited her in commanding Israel to treat the Midianites as enemies (Numbers 25).

debir_995.name: Debir
debir_995.who: The Amorite king of Eglon who joined a coalition against Gibeon and was defeated by Joshua.
key: Adoni-zedek of Jerusalem called him to join in attacking Gibeon for making peace with Israel (Joshua 10).
After the battle he and four other kings hid in a cave at Makkedah (Joshua 10).
Joshua brought them out, put them to death, and hung them on trees (Joshua 10).

demas_1006.name: Demas
demas_1006.who: A coworker of Paul who later deserted him for love of the present world.
key: He sent greetings to the Colossians along with Luke (Colossians 4).
Paul named him among his fellow workers when writing to Philemon (Philemon 1).
Loving this present world, he deserted Paul and went to Thessalonica (2 Timothy 4).

demetrius_1007.name: Demetrius
demetrius_1007.who: A silversmith of Ephesus who made silver shrines of Artemis and stirred up a riot against Paul.
key: His trade brought much business to the craftsmen of Ephesus (Acts 19).
He warned them Paul's preaching endangered their trade and Artemis's temple, and the city filled with confusion (Acts 19).
The town clerk told him to bring any complaint before the courts and dismissed the assembly (Acts 19).
A different Demetrius, well spoken of by everyone, is commended by John (3 John 1).

dionysius_1013.name: Dionysius
dionysius_1013.who: A member of the Areopagus council in Athens who believed after hearing Paul.
key: He heard Paul proclaim the resurrection before the Areopagus in Athens (Acts 17).
He joined Paul and believed, along with a woman named Damaris and others (Acts 17).

diotrephes_1014.name: Diotrephes
diotrephes_1014.who: A church leader who loved to be first and refused to welcome John's messengers.
key: John says he likes to put himself first and does not acknowledge John's authority (3 John 1).
He spoke wicked nonsense, refused traveling brothers, and expelled those who welcomed them (3 John 1).
John said he would bring up what Diotrephes was doing when he came (3 John 1).

dodanim_1018.name: Dodanim
dodanim_1018.who: A son of Javan and descendant of Japheth, listed in the Table of Nations among the coastland peoples.
key: He is listed among the sons of Javan, son of Japheth (Genesis 10).
Chronicles gives the name as Rodanim in the same list (1 Chronicles 1).

doeg_1023.name: Doeg
doeg_1023.who: An Edomite, chief of Saul's herdsmen, who betrayed Ahimelech and killed the priests of Nob.
key: He was at Nob, detained before the LORD, when David received bread and Goliath's sword (1 Samuel 21).
He told Saul he had seen Ahimelech help David (1 Samuel 22).
When Saul's guards refused, Doeg killed eighty-five priests and struck down the town of Nob (1 Samuel 22).
The title of Psalm 52 links that psalm to Doeg's report to Saul (Psalm 52).

dorcas_2810.name: Tabitha
dorcas_2810.who: A disciple in Joppa known for good works and charity, whom Peter raised from the dead.
key: She was full of good works and acts of charity among the believers in Joppa (Acts 9).
She fell sick and died, and the disciples sent to Lydda for Peter (Acts 9).
Weeping widows showed Peter the tunics and garments she had made (Acts 9).
Peter prayed and told her to arise; she sat up, and many believed in the Lord (Acts 9).

drusilla_1024.name: Drusilla
drusilla_1024.who: The Jewish wife of the Roman governor Felix, who heard Paul speak in Caesarea.
key: She came with Felix, who sent for Paul and heard him speak about faith in Christ Jesus (Acts 24).
As Paul reasoned about righteousness, self-control, and judgment, Felix grew alarmed and sent him away (Acts 24).

ebal_1026.name: Ebal
ebal_1026.who: A Horite of Seir, son of Shobal, listed among the early inhabitants of Edom.
key: He is listed among the sons of Shobal, son of Seir the Horite (Genesis 36).
Chronicles repeats him among the descendants of Seir (1 Chronicles 1).

eder_1035.name: Eder
eder_1035.who: A Levite of the clan of Merari, son of Mushi, listed in David's Levite divisions.
key: He is listed among the sons of Mushi when David organized the Levites (1 Chronicles 23).
He is named again when the Levites cast lots for duties as the priests did (1 Chronicles 24).

eglon_1037.name: Eglon
eglon_1037.who: A king of Moab who oppressed Israel for eighteen years until Ehud killed him.
key: Because Israel did evil, the LORD strengthened Eglon, who with Ammon and Amalek took the city of palms (Judges 3).
Israel served him eighteen years (Judges 3).
Ehud brought him tribute, then stabbed the very fat king in his cool roof chamber (Judges 3).
Israel then defeated Moab, and the land had rest eighty years (Judges 3).

elah_1045.name: Elah
elah_1045.who: A king of Israel, son of Baasha, who reigned two years before Zimri assassinated him.
key: He became king at Tirzah in Asa's twenty-sixth year and reigned two years (1 Kings 16).
While he was drunk in his steward's house, his commander Zimri struck him down (1 Kings 16).
Zimri then destroyed Baasha's house, as the prophet Jehu had foretold (1 Kings 16).

elah_1046.name: Elah
elah_1046.who: The father of Hoshea, the last king of the northern kingdom of Israel.
key: His son Hoshea conspired against King Pekah, killed him, and became king (2 Kings 15).
Hoshea son of Elah reigned nine years in Samaria until Assyria captured it (2 Kings 17).

eldaah_1057.name: Eldaah
eldaah_1057.who: A son of Midian and grandson of Abraham through Keturah.
key: He is listed among the sons of Midian, son of Abraham and Keturah (Genesis 25).
Chronicles repeats him among Keturah's descendants (1 Chronicles 1).

eldad_1058.name: Eldad
eldad_1058.who: One of the seventy elders of Israel who prophesied in the camp in Moses' day.
key: He was registered among the seventy elders but remained in the camp (Numbers 11).
The Spirit rested on him and Medad, and they prophesied in the camp (Numbers 11).
When Joshua urged Moses to stop them, Moses wished all the LORD's people were prophets (Numbers 11).
